correctness.rationale: A table with all minimal keys the 3-sets has each distinct row pair agreeing on at most two coordinates, and every coordinate pair is exactly the agreement set of a row pair. Thus C(m,2)>=C(n,2), m>=n. At diagonal m=n, all row pairs have exactly two agreements and are bijective witnesses for the column pairs. Encoding each column by its canonical partition of m rows into <=3 values gives a mask on row pairs. Pairwise column-mask intersections must have size exactly one, and no row-pair edge lies in three masks. Exhaustive increasing-index DFS on all canonical ternary partitions for m=3,5,6 (respectively 4,40,121 possibilities) finds no m-column family; independently written direct DFS reproduces zero terminal solutions with nonidentical search-node counts. Explicit displayed 4x4, 6x5 and 7x7 row witnesses and the 3- and 6-column projections pass all exact agreement tests. The previously proved upper length f(3,3)=7 handles n>=8. Therefore minima n=3..7 are [4,4,6,7,7]. Unlike a partial search, the canonical partition enumeration and coverage of every diagonal candidate are mathematically justified.

originality.rationale: Chee–Zhang–Zhang prove the maximum admissible ternary attribute length seven and exhibit a seven-row seven-column Armstrong code. Katona–Sali–Schewe give general coding/bounded domain lower bounds and m>=n, while older Beeri–Dowd–Fagin–Statman treat general Armstrong relation sizes. The candidate’s strict diagonal impossibility at n=5,6 and complete minimum-row function [4,4,6,7,7] are absent from the inspected principal papers. These finite exact naturally parameterized minima are not known-table repetition: n=5,6 require exhaustive partition obstructions.
